meta.note: Worldwide figures for 2020, written by hand from Pew's published report. Pew does not publish new global estimates monthly, so check data/faiths.json when Pew releases a new dataset.

faiths.s: A faith centered on the life and teachings of Jesus of Nazareth, which began in the 1st century in the Roman province of Judea.
faiths.fun: The Bible has been translated, in whole or in part, into well over 3,000 languages.
faiths.special: Christianity is the world's largest religion, and sub-Saharan Africa now has more Christians than any other region.
known: Origin: Judea, in the 1st century.
Holy book: the Bible.
Main branches: Catholic, Protestant and Orthodox.
Followers in 2020: about 2.3 billion, 28.8% of the world.

faiths.s: A faith that follows the message revealed to the Prophet Muhammad in 7th-century Arabia, with the Quran as its holy book.
faiths.fun: The Islamic calendar follows the moon, so the month of Ramadan arrives about 11 days earlier each year on the usual calendar.
faiths.special: Muslims were the fastest-growing major religious group from 2010 to 2020, growing by 347 million people.
known: Origin: the Arabian Peninsula, in the 7th century.
Holy book: the Quran.
Main branches: Sunni and Shia.
Followers in 2020: about 2 billion, 25.6% of the world.

faiths.s: One of the world's oldest living religions, with roots in the Indian subcontinent and a wide range of traditions, texts and practices.
faiths.fun: Diwali, the festival of lights, is celebrated by Hindus and also by Sikhs, Jains and some Buddhists.
faiths.special: About 95% of the world's Hindus live in India.
known: Origin: the Indian subcontinent, thousands of years ago.
Texts: the Vedas, the Upanishads and the Bhagavad Gita.
Followers in 2020: about 1.2 billion, 14.9% of the world.

faiths.s: A tradition based on the teachings of Siddhartha Gautama, the Buddha, who lived in northern India about 2,500 years ago.
faiths.fun: The word Buddha means awakened one.
faiths.special: Buddhists were the only major group with fewer people in 2020 than in 2010.
known: Origin: northern India, about 2,500 years ago.
Main traditions: Theravada, Mahayana and Vajrayana.
Followers in 2020: about 324 million, 4.1% of the world.

faiths.s: One of the oldest monotheistic faiths, rooted in the Hebrew Bible and in the covenant between God and the people of Israel.
faiths.fun: The Jewish day begins at sundown, so the Sabbath, Shabbat, starts on Friday evening.
faiths.special: Israel is home to 6.8 million Jews, which is 46% of the world's Jews.
known: Origin: ancient Israel and Judah, in the Middle East.
Texts: the Hebrew Bible (the Tanakh) and the Talmud.
Followers in 2020: about 14.8 million, about 0.2% of the world.

faiths.pl: counted by Pew with other religions (2.2% of the world)
faiths.s: A faith founded by Guru Nanak in the Punjab region in the late 15th century, centered on one God, equality and service.
faiths.fun: Sikh gurdwaras serve a free community meal, called langar, to everyone who comes, whatever their background.
faiths.special: The Guru Granth Sahib, the Sikh holy book, is treated as the final living guru.
known: Origin: the Punjab region, in the late 15th century.
Holy book: the Guru Granth Sahib.
Followers: Pew counts Sikhs in its other religions group, which is 2.2% of the world together with folk religions and others.

faiths.s: A wide group of traditions, such as Jainism, the Baháʼí Faith and many Indigenous and ancestral practices, counted together in Pew's data.
faiths.fun: Many of these traditions are passed down through stories, ceremonies and songs rather than written books.
faiths.special: Together with Sikhs, these traditions were 2.2% of the world's people in 2020.
known: Origin: all over the world.
Examples: Jainism, the Baháʼí Faith and many Indigenous traditions.
Followers in 2020: 2.2% of the world, counted together with Sikhs.

faiths.s: People who identify as atheist, agnostic or with no particular religion. Many still hold spiritual beliefs.
faiths.fun: The group is often called the nones, because on surveys they answer none when asked their religion.
faiths.special: The unaffiliated were 24.2% of the world in 2020, the third-largest group after Christians and Muslims.
known: Includes: atheists, agnostics and people with no particular religion.
Followers in 2020: about 1.9 billion, 24.2% of the world.
